candidate.answerReason: The bases sum to 56 yards. Their possible unordered pairs are (8,48), (16,40), and (24,32).

methods.label: List the possible base pairs
methods.explanation:
The area formula first tells us the sum of the bases. If their lengths are \(u\) and \(v\) yards, then
\[
1400=\frac{(u+v)50}{2},
\qquad u+v=56.
\]
To avoid counting a pair twice, let \(u\) be the smaller base. Both bases are positive, so \(0<u\le 28\). The only multiples of \(8\) in this range are \(8,16,24\), giving the pairs
\[
(8,48),\qquad(16,40),\qquad(24,32).
\]
Each pair has positive bases divisible by \(8\), and each gives the required area with altitude \(50\). Every possible smaller base has been included, and reversing a pair does not give a new solution. Thus there are \(\boxed{3}\) solutions, choice D.
